text: Cooking changes basic items into full-flavored plates. Simmering involves holding food in liquid like broth or water using low heat for an extended duration. This technique preserves nutrients and tastes while improving texture and scent. Seasoning is the last action, letting you define the meal's flavor. You must balance tastes by adding correct levels of salt, pepper, herbs, and spices. Every bite becomes tasty and full. Learning how to simmer and season well lets you make many healthy, appealing dishes.
